# Dukkhāhārakathā (Kv 2.6)

**ID:** Kv 2.6
**Section:** Kathāvatthu (kv)

**Title (Pali):** Dukkhāhārakathā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul9.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dukkhāhārakathā* (Kv 2.6) is the sixth discourse of the second chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, an Abhidhamma treatise preserved in the Pali Canon. The debate centers on the thesis that "sorrow as sustenance" or suffering as an intake (*dukkhāhāra*) constitutes a factor of the Path (*magganga*) and is comprised within the Path (*maggapariyāpanna*) [Bareau 1955]. The refutation demonstrates that if such an intake of suffering were indeed a path-factor, then anyone uttering the exclamation "O suffering!" (*dukkhanti*), including ordinary worldlings (*puthujjana*), matricides, parricides, murderers of arahants, and those who cause the shedding of a Buddha's blood, would thereby be developing the Path [Bareau 1955].

**Sources**

- [Bareau 1955] André Bareau, Les sectes bouddhiques du Petit Véhicule (1955) — Doctrinal summary of the thesis and refutation regarding whether dukkhāhāra is a limb of the Path.
